title: Gaussian basis of the empirical potential (Gaussian T)
purpose: Exercises the Gaussian representation of the empirical potential (EP) in the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005], selected with `Gaussian` in the `.pcof` file instead of the default Poisson (power-exponential) functions [@epsrmanual]. The basis determines how the difference between data and simulation is expanded in Q and converted into an r-space potential.
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. For this case the EP is a sum of Gaussians centred at d = m·pdstep with width `psigma2`; in Q space each basis function is sin(Qd)/(Qd)·exp(-(Q·sigma)²/2).
inputs: Made from EPSR-test with `scripts/make_case.py`: `.pcof` keyword `Gaussian T` instead of `Poisson`. The EP coefficients fitted with the Poisson basis in EPSR-test are kept and reinterpreted in the Gaussian basis.
verification: The value `T` is rewritten as `Gaussian` after pass 1, so passes 2 and 3 test the second accepted spelling. The basis is active: the README reports an EP energy of about 99 compared with 3.7 in the Poisson run. The README reports a gcov check of the Fortran covering `inita`, `generate_ep`/`calc_gaussr_grad` and `ptgnsq`/`calc_gaussq`.
notes: `rbroad`, `dmax` and `rho` are not used by the Gaussian basis routines, and with `rmin = 0` `ncfirst` is never touched.
